Several people have asked how I prepare lecture notes in HTML and PDF. Here’s an overview of the workflow. This is *slightly* different from how I do it day to day because I use a “book” project rather than a “website” project, but the principles are the same.

Here’s an [example site](https://phajy.github.io/andys-quarto-example/geodesics.html).

- I keep notes in a GitHub repository for version history and backup. This also works well for collaborative projects. You do not need to use [GitHub](https://github.com/).
- Notes are written in [Markdown](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html), using [LaTeX](https://www.latex-project.org/) syntax for mathematics.
- Markdown is rendered to HTML, PDF, and other formats with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/). Quarto can also embed executable code blocks — something I plan to use more.
- I use [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) with the [Quarto extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=quarto.quarto).
- Lecture notes can be hosted on a University service or on GitHub Pages. I’ve tested GitHub Pages publishing and it works well.

## Set up an empty GitHub repository

Start with a blank repository containing a `README.md` and a `LICENSE`. I’ve used the MIT license. Alternatively, create the Quarto project first and push everything afterwards.

The example repository is [andys-quarto-example](https://github.com/phajy/andys-quarto-example).

## Install Quarto

Follow the [Quarto get-started instructions](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/). On a Mac with Homebrew: `brew install --cask quarto`.

## Editor setup

Install the [Quarto VS Code / Cursor extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=quarto.quarto).

## Start a Quarto website project

You can use “Quarto: Create New Project” and choose “Website Project”, or add a few files by hand:

- `_quarto.yml` — project configuration
- `index.md` — home page
- `about.md` — another page
- `styles.css` — optional styling

See the files in the [example repository](https://github.com/phajy/andys-quarto-example).

## Publishing

Follow the [Quarto GitHub Pages instructions](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html). For a simple start you can render to `docs/` and deploy from that folder; a GitHub Action is usually better for keeping the site up to date automatically.

Published example: [https://phajy.github.io/andys-quarto-example/](https://phajy.github.io/andys-quarto-example/).

## Add content

Headings, figures, and mathematics follow standard Quarto Markdown. For example:

```markdown
## Parallel-transport and geodesics

![Parallel transport of a vector.](parallel_transport.png){width=300 #fig-parallel-transport}

We can use parallel transport to construct *geodesics*:

$$
\begin{aligned}
    \pmb{\nabla}_{\vec u} {\vec u} &= 0
\end{aligned}
$$
```

More in the [Quarto Markdown documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html).
